chapter: The Latin scene and business of the 1940s-70s
title: Japan tour and promoters
summary: He recounts the Japan trip, his booker, and promoters' power.

blocks.x: Musical-wise more than anything else, he was working, doing the same (unintelligible). I'm going to Japan because they sent for me. And Copellor going with me,

he's my booker. Copellor going with me there, and the time it started, he started looking for my business. He was so busy trying to set the (unintelligible). I got back to America, (unintelligible) Japan is unbelievable. So about four months later or five months or six months later, (inaudible).

They sit down and talk for two weeks, and the guy that bought it (unintelligible). They go from there to Hong Kong and set me up, they go to Manila and set me up. The whole -- to make the story short, there was a (inaudible). From then on, (unintelligible). About six months ago, I said this is ridiculous, this is unbelievable.
This happened during the late '60s or early '70s, right?
Right, but what I mean is, the --

There was no more competition. They me in the Palladium, they even got it so they (inaudible). I read the whole scene on the wall. They were trying to create something. (Unintelligible.) I mean, let's face it. It's about time somebody said something and I'll be the one to say it. Chito won't say it, but I'll say it.
Definitely. It's been said, other musicians have also said that there's a lot too much power on the (unintelligible) circuit of a few promoters, you've got
and then as far as promoters are concerned, you've always had only two or three, right?
Yeah. So it was a combination of this and that again, (unintelligible).

And see who's who, here. (Unintelligible.) But they never stopped (unintelligible) with Chito. Right now, he (unintelligible). I said, you got this trip. I ain't going to make no trip. But I'm going to recommend that you tell your men, if you need me, tell me when you're going into rehearsal and (inaudible). And this is a big trip and it means so much for you and everybody else.
